summary: M0 model-only verdict: CONTAIN @ 0.92. Confirmed account takeover for o.polat@aegean.edu. The user's normal baseline is twice-daily logins from Manisa, Turkey — 09:00 on the university network (AS-AEGEAN-EDU, device DEV-H05-L, mail/lms, no MFA) and 21:00 on home ISP Superonline (device DEV-H05-P, mail, MFA-approved). On 2026-10-09 23:40 there is an IMAP failure from 203.0.113.17 (DigitalOcean, Amsterdam), immediately followed by repeated IMAP successes from that same cloud IP with no device_id and no MFA prompt. Then on 2026-10-11 there are repeated IMAP successes from a second cloud host, 192.0.2.66 (Hetzner, Falkenstein, DE), again with no device and no MFA. IMAP auth from cloud IPs without MFA or a known device is inconsistent with the legitimate user's pattern and indicates use of stolen credentials/app-password to bypass MFA. Corroborating the compromise, a mail event at 2026-10-11 01:20:30 shows an inbox rule deleting items into the Deleted Items folder via API — consistent with an attacker covering tracks. This meets the contain threshold (confirmed account takeover), not merely monitor/benign.
limitations: M0 ablation: Nemotron alone, no tools, no Critic, no Risk Gate, no DQ. Not a product configuration.
